s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple bluish, partially keratotic skin lesions with slow growth, associated with vascular malformations and neurological deficits
salient_findings: Bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
key_facts: Female patient in her early 50s
Multiple skin lesions on the lower legs
Lesions have been growing slowly since age 24
Lesions bleed occasionally after trauma
Patient uses a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia
History of intracranial hemorrhage
Recurrent seizures at age 4
Lipolymphedema of the lower legs
Family history of similar conditions
Father died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography showed intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations
Histopathology revealed dilated venous-like malformations with thrombosis
Genetic testing detected a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

shortlist.label: Cerebral cavernous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: KRIT1 variant and history of intracranial hemorrhage

shortlist.label: Venous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Sonography and histopathology showing dilated venous-like malformations

shortlist.label: Fabry disease
shortlist.why_kept: Vascular malformations and potential neurological involvement

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Vascular malformations and history of seizures

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, which is a known cause of cerebral cavernous malformations, along with the patient's history of intracranial hemorrhage and family history of similar conditions, supports this diagnosis. The skin lesions are also consistent with cutaneous vascular malformations associated with cerebral cavernous malformations.

rejected.label: Venous malformation
rejected.why: While sonography and histopathology show venous-like malformations, the genetic testing and family history point towards a more specific diagnosis of cerebral cavernous malformation.

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with port-wine stains, varicose veins, and bony and soft tissue hypertrophy, which are not all mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Fabry disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of the typical symptoms of Fabry disease, such as pain in the hands and feet, gastrointestinal disturbances, or characteristic skin lesions.

rejected.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by a port-wine stain in the distribution of the trigeminal nerve, which is not described in the vignette, and typically does not present with the same type of skin lesions or family history as seen in this patient.
